solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detective on estate arresting party who's cruel to animals

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the car holds the party inside it

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, so CAR
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A police detective at a housing estate arrests a reveller known for animal cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here: in a down clue it puts the detective above the car.
explanation.definitionFit: The horseman in a bullfight lances the bull to weaken it, a role many see as animal cruelty.

clue.text: In conclusion, town's first Republican leaving elite group unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so what remains is rearranged
leaving says those letters go out of the phrase elite group
first picks the opening letter of the word town's

explanation.surface: A town's top Republican quits an elite circle that is left unsettled at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T and R from ELITE GROUP leaves ELIEGOUP, which 'unsettled' rearranges. The definition reads as a phrase: an epilogue is what comes in conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing section of a book or play, the part that comes at the end.

clue.text: King and queen welcoming run on foreign currency

indicators.note: welcoming means letting in, so king and queen take the run and the on between them

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal couple greet a run on some foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Kroner are the currency units of Denmark and Norway, money from abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: A genius worked round finale of Lord's prayer

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the next piece
worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters of A genius are reshaped
the finale of a word is its last letter, here of Lord

explanation.surface: A clever person wrapped up the Lord's Prayer at its end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Lord stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition; only the last letter of Lord, D, is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is a prayer in the Christian Mass.

clue.text: Plate of meat almost held up by topless girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, being held up by puts the meat above the girl
almost means the last letter of the meat is dropped

parts.note: lamb is a meat

indicators.note: topless means the girl's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Nina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A plate of meat is carried aloft by a girl in a state of undress.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer or plate, of bone, rock or metal.

clue.text: Trot around base is hated

indicators.note: around says the red goes around the next word

parts.note: a Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a red
base means vile, low

explanation.surface: A trot round a base, like a baseball runner, is despised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' looks like a jog, but it is the political sense: a Trotskyist, so RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviled means vilified and abused, treated with loathing.

clue.text: Traveller gets help about pad in US

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the traveller and help are read backwards

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales rep
aid is help

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman gets assistance finding lodgings in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' looks like a flat, but it is an absorbent pad: Americans call a nappy a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaper is the American word for a baby's nappy, an absorbent pad.

clue.text: A setter is normally this shabby

definitions.meaning: a setter is a breed of dog, and dogs normally have ears
shabby means worn and tatty, like a book with turned-down page corners

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is usually scruffy-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with folded corners look worn, so the word describes anything well-thumbed and tatty.

clue.text: Fail to include son — fancy daughter being let down

indicators.note: to include means the failing word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to die is to fail, as an engine dies
a fancy is an illusion, something imagined

explanation.surface: Not finding a place for a son while imagining a daughter leaves one disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disillusioned is being disappointed, having lost a cherished belief.

clue.text: Fence complains bitterly about criminals having run away

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the complaining goes round the rest

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly

indicators.note: having run away means the run letter leaves the gang

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A receiver of stolen goods grumbles that the crooks have fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like the criminal receiver, which fits the crooks, but it is the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Railings are a barrier of upright bars, a kind of fence.

clue.text: Inflammation left one in situ, being withdrawn

indicators.note: in places the left and one inside the turned word
withdrawn means pulled back, so the word situ is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An inflammation was left alone where it was, then receded.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing SITU gives UTIS, and LI goes in after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulitis is inflammation of the gums, the medical term for gingivitis.

clue.text: English Literature initially taken by person following verse

indicators.note: taken by puts the person following first, with the two letters after

parts.note: one who dogs, tails someone, is a dogger

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of English and Literature

explanation.surface: A student of English Literature first takes on a stalker poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: the follower comes first, then E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is comic or badly written verse.

clue.text: Artist's pay rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a reward is payment

explanation.surface: A painter's fee has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Artist stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws pictures can be called a drawer, an artist.

clue.text: Turns partner back on when wearing tight suit

indicators.note: back means the partner's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lover is a partner

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters of on and suit are in disarray

explanation.surface: A partner's ardour is rekindled at the sight of a figure-hugging outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' seems to describe the suit but is the drunken anagram signal; 'when wearing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolutions are complete rotations, turns of a wheel or engine.

clue.text: Damn wool irritated great- granny?

indicators.note: irritated means disturbed or upset, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: An elderly knitter curses her irritating wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a great-grandmother is an old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-grandmother is an elderly lady, an example of the type, signalled by the query.

clue.text: Contract manuscript torn-up in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly placed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A contract document has been mistakenly ripped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a legal document, but it is a bid in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a no-trumps contract is a bid to play with no trump suit.

clue.text: Free one who is oppressed by dues on a regular basis

indicators.note: in a down clue, being oppressed by puts the alternate letters on top of the liver
on a regular basis picks every other letter of dues

parts.note: one who is, someone living, is a liver

explanation.surface: Release someone weighed down by regular subscription payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who' is followed by 'is' working twice: 'one who is' is a LIVER, someone who lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver is to set free or rescue, as in deliver us from evil.

clue.text: Burglary becoming known before it finishes

indicators.note: before it finishes means stopping short of the last letter

parts.note: news breaking is news becoming known

explanation.surface: A burglary is reported before it is even over.
explanation.definitionFit: A break-in is a forced entry to a building, usually to steal.

clue.text: Hostility stopping Labour gain

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the hostility goes inside

parts.note: the Labour Party is the red party in Britain
war is hostility

explanation.surface: Infighting stops the Labour Party making headway.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a gain or benefit received in return for something.

clue.text: Brutal change Stalin made after repeated shelling

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters left are rearranged
shelling twice strips the two outer letters from each end of Stalin made

explanation.surface: Stalin's alterations were brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link; STALINMADE shelled twice loses S, T, D and E, leaving ALINMA to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means physical and beastly, as in brutal animal instincts.

clue.text: Green activist on vacation shut up housing

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so the shut-up word contains the rest

parts.note: to immure is to shut up or imprison

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of activist remain

explanation.surface: A green campaigner on holiday is locked up in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks political beside 'activist', but here it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or unripe, like someone not fully grown up.

clue.text: For example, access bank loss after this recollection

parts.words: For example, access bank loss after this
parts.note: the words access, bank and loss each follow this word to make a common phrase

explanation.walkthrough: Each example word completes a phrase with the answer in front: random-... access, ... bank, ... loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory is something remembered, a recollection of the past.

clue.text: Drive courageous type almost to accept offer

indicators.note: to accept means taking in, so the shortened word holds the offer
almost means the brave type loses its last letter

parts.note: a lion is a brave person
a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: Drive a brave person nearly to the point of taking a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a verb but is the noun: sexual drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual urge or desire, a basic drive.

clue.text: Retreating soldiers save "a line" for sedative

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the soldiers are read in reverse

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men
save means except, which is but

explanation.surface: Retreating troops keep a single line of tranquilliser in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Nembutal is a brand of pentobarbital, a barbiturate used as a sedative.

clue.text: Kind of support English fête in top

indicators.note: in places the English fête inside the top

parts.note: a lid is a top
a gala is a fête, a festive event

explanation.surface: Some sort of assistance for an English summer fair, wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is state funding of legal advice for those who cannot pay, a form of assistance.

clue.text: Settled record when in charge?

indicators.note: in places the record inside the charge

parts.note: a raid is a charge, an attack
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record was settled when someone was in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests responsibility, but it is an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is repaid has been settled, paid back.
